routines.name: AddressSet1
routines.evidence: `movi COINS_M1,a0 / move a0,@_coin_addr,L` and the same for the switch, sound and counter addresses -- one of four I/O base-address maps the security chip selects between through trap 3. There is no coin door or PIC here.

routines.name: AddressSet2
routines.evidence: See AddressSet1: the second I/O base-address map.

routines.name: AddressSet3
routines.evidence: See AddressSet1: the third I/O base-address map.

routines.name: AddressSet4
routines.evidence: See AddressSet1: the fourth I/O base-address map.

routines.name: BEGINOBJ_TBL
routines.evidence: Creates an object from a table of its parameters.

routines.name: BLACKOUT
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It blanks the screen behind a message.

routines.name: BONUS_MESS
routines.evidence: The source's own comment: 'Process which displays high risk - 2x damage & possibly move name'.

routines.name: CLR_SCRN
routines.evidence: Blanks DISPLAYON and clears the frame buffer.

routines.name: CREATE_TIMEOUT
routines.evidence: LIFEBAR.ASM:4876. The TIME OUT graphic the main loop creates when the round clock expires: a sound, a BEGINOBJ at [200,300] with an upward OYVEL, two FX_PID processes copying and moving it, then four passes of TIMEOUT_FLASH_ANIM through ANIM_CROWD. Object and animation drawing throughout; what it is a consequence OF -- the clock reaching zero and the round being decided by LIFEBAR.ASM:5149 set_winner's #tmout rule -- is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_match_clock.h.

routines.name: CREATE_URN
routines.evidence: Puts the Undertaker's urn on the ladder screen. Screen construction; the ladder state it draws is wm/pregame.h's.

routines.name: DELETE_ANY_OFF_TOP
routines.evidence: HSTD.ASM:531. Deletes objects once the scroll has carried them above the screen.

routines.name: DO_REVERSAL_MESS
routines.evidence: A display process. Its one piece of logic -- RND_AWARD a8,REVERSAL_AWD -- is translated in wm/award.h; the rest is the message object and its voice call.

routines.name: DO_RIGHT_MUSIC
routines.evidence: Picks the music for the round about to start and hands it to SNDSND.

routines.name: DO_RIGHT_MUSIC2
routines.evidence: The same for the second half of a match.

routines.name: DO_SET_IMAGES
routines.evidence: WRESTLE.ASM. Walks a wrestler's MAX_PIECES object list and points each piece at its image for the current frame -- the multi-piece sprite assembly a WIMP wrestler is drawn from. wm/match_display.h decides the ORDER and the layers this would build; nothing plots them yet.

routines.name: DRKTRPLTP
routines.evidence: Not a routine at all: `.word 31` followed by thirty-two colour words -- a darkened palette table for the screen fade. The disassembly's label scan cannot tell a table from an entry point; this one is a table.

routines.name: FIRSTATT_MESS
routines.evidence: Puts the FIRSTATT message up over the player who landed the first blow.

routines.name: GAME_BEATEN
routines.evidence: Puts the 'game beaten' plaque up. The decisions around it are translated elsewhere; the object creation and layout are the display layer's.

routines.name: GENERIC_DISPLAY
routines.evidence: The attract mode's shared page frame: background, border, and the timed wait. The attract sequence's order and timing are wm/arcade/wmania_attract_core.h's; these build the pages.

routines.name: GetSoundRev
routines.evidence: `move @_coin_counter_addr,a0,L / movi 030h,a1 / move a1,*a0,W` -- writes a command to the sound board and reads its revision back. A DCS board handshake.

routines.name: ICON_SPARKLE
routines.evidence: Sparkles on a power-up icon; it checks @reduce_bog first and dies rather than adding objects when the frame rate is already suffering.

routines.name: INTIO
routines.evidence: `movi HESYNC,b2 / movi gspioinit_t,b0` -- loads the TMS34010's video timing registers from a table. The N64's video is libdragon's.

routines.name: InitAddresses
routines.evidence: The default I/O base-address map (COINS, SWITCH and the rest at their unremapped addresses).

routines.name: InitPIC
routines.evidence: Initialises the PIC microcontroller that owns the coin door, the switches and the real-time clock. There is no PIC in this port.

routines.name: JUDDER_SHADOW
routines.evidence: HSTD.ASM. A FLASH_PID process that shakes the drop shadow behind the high-score heading. A CREATE, a loop and an object offset.

routines.name: MAKE_UP_LOGO
routines.evidence: Builds one logo object from a table of image, X and Y, offset by the caller's a3/a5. The attract sequence's order and timing are wm/arcade/wmania_attract_core.h's; these build the pages.

routines.name: MOVE_ALL_OBJS_UP
routines.evidence: HSTD.ASM:512. Gives every object on the high-score page an upward Y velocity so the table scrolls off. Object motion, nothing else.

routines.name: MOVE_NAME_ANNC
routines.evidence: Slides the wrestler name plates in at the announcement.

routines.name: ONE_BALL
routines.evidence: One of the attract sequence's animated pages. The attract sequence's order and timing are wm/arcade/wmania_attract_core.h's; these build the pages.

routines.name: PUT_UP_PROGRESS
routines.evidence: Builds the whole progress-ladder screen. Screen construction; the ladder state it draws is wm/pregame.h's.

routines.name: RemapIO
routines.evidence: MAIN.ASM. Moves the I/O window in the address map. Its one call site in WRESTLE.ASM's main loop is commented out, under the author's own question: "isn't there a less obvious place that we can remap the IO ???"

routines.name: SET_FLASHING
routines.evidence: Starts the combo-flash process and its sound. The COMBO_FLASH_FLAG guard it wraps is the actor's combo_flash field.

routines.name: SNDSND
routines.evidence: The DCS sound board's own protocol. An N64 has no ADSP-2105 and no sample ROM to drive with it; what crosses the boundary instead is the 16-bit CALL the board would have been handed, which wm/arcade/wm_arcade_sound.h's mixer decides on and wm/audio.h's queue carries to the platform. DCSSOUND.ASM:2519 SNDSND is send_code_a3: refuse if @SOUNDSUP, refuse a negative (null) call, then write the call's high byte and low byte to the latch with a poll_sirq wait after each. The two refusals are real and are translated in the mixer; the two byte writes are the board.

routines.name: SPECIAL_DISPLAY_INIT
routines.evidence: `pushst / dint / movi DIE+X2E,a0` -- programs the video controller registers for the special display mode. Video setup is libdragon's.

routines.name: SPECIAL_WIPEOUT
routines.evidence: UTIL.ASM:113. WIPEOUT2 then a jump to SPECIAL_DISPLAY_INIT -- the same reset with a different display mode after it.

routines.name: START_HI_FLASHES
routines.evidence: Starts the flashers on the ladder's highlighted entries. Screen construction; the ladder state it draws is wm/pregame.h's.

routines.name: STOP_ALL_OBJS
routines.evidence: HSTD.ASM:501. Zeroes every object's velocity -- the other half of the scroll.

routines.name: STRCNRM_1
routines.evidence: One of six four-instruction entry points into the shared string printer (STRLNRM, STRCNRM, STRRNRM and the rest): it loads DMAWNZ|M_NOCOLL, sets the justification code to 1 for centred, copies a6 into a5 for the multi-colour path and jumps to stringr1_1. The justification and colour handling are the text layer's; wm/arcade/wm_arcade_string.h carries the font metrics side.

routines.name: SecFuncCheck
routines.evidence: Walks SecFuncTable comparing each security-function entry point against its expected value, to catch a tampered security chip. Its first instruction in the shipped build is `rets`: the check is disabled. There is no security chip here either way.

routines.name: SetAddresses
routines.evidence: `move a0,a0 / jrn _invalid / cmpi 4,a0` then a jump into AddressSet1-4. The dispatcher for the I/O remap; nothing to remap here.

routines.name: THIS_GAME_IS_BEATEN
routines.evidence: `CLR A0 / MOVE A0,@PSTATUS / movi INGAMEOVER,a14 / move a14,@GAMSTATE` then the game-over process. The state change is three stores; the screen it puts up is the rest of it. The decisions around it are translated elsewhere; the object creation and layout are the display layer's.

routines.name: UNDBLU_P
routines.evidence: WRESPAL.ASM:136. One of the Undertaker's palettes. The palette corpus is extracted wholesale by tools/wlpal.py into src/generated/palettes.c, so this is a row in generated data rather than a routine anything calls.

routines.name: VOLBTN_PRESS
routines.evidence: DCSSOUND.ASM:2564. The cabinet's two volume buttons behind the coin door, read straight off the coin port and written to the board's volume register. There is no coin door on an N64 and no operator volume setting for it to adjust.

routines.name: WARMSET
routines.evidence: The warm-reset entry: DINT, the two SETF field definitions, the stack pointer, InitPIC, POWERCMOS (skipped under DEBUG with the source's own note "This takes all day to run. leave it out until we ship") and init_all. TMS34010 state and cabinet hardware.

routines.name: WDOGDIS
routines.evidence: `.if TUNIT=0` around a write to the watchdog register. A hardware watchdog this port does not have.

routines.name: WHERE_WRESTLMANIA_SPARKLES
routines.evidence: The sparkle positions on the WrestleMania logo.

routines.name: WIPEOUT
routines.evidence: UTIL.ASM:122. dirq_wait, display_init, then pal_init inside a dint, and fall through to WIPEOUT2: reset the machine between screens. Every line is the cabinet's display processor or its palette RAM.

routines.name: WIPEOUT2
routines.evidence: UTIL.ASM:136. The rest of the reset: zero a dozen globals, KILALL every process, ZERO_BITS the bitmap, dpageflip_off, then write SYSCTRL from SYSCOPY (with the WWFUNIT variant that leaves the 7-segment LED alone). Process and hardware state this port does not have.

routines.name: ZERO_BITS
routines.evidence: UTIL.ASM:103. Clears BAKBITS -- 10000/16 words of the machine's own bitmap RAM -- with a word-store loop. There is no BAKBITS on an N64.

routines.name: _AlarmClock
routines.evidence: Called by the display interrupt when the RTC seconds roll over; walks ALARM_TAB firing whatever is due. The clock it reads is the PIC's.

routines.name: _GetTime
routines.evidence: Reads the real-time clock through the PIC, with @_auto_update_save around it so the display interrupt does not race the read.

routines.name: _aquire_time
routines.evidence: `movi 011h,a0 / move a0,@PIC_COMMAND,W` -- asks the PIC to latch the current time.

routines.name: _get_time
routines.evidence: Copies the eight latched time bytes out of the PIC into _tseconds and its neighbours.

routines.name: _set_time
routines.evidence: Writes _rtc_seconds through _rtc_year back to the PIC. The operator's clock-setting screen.

routines.name: addbrt_ae
routines.evidence: PAL.ASM:1009. A CREATE0'd process that ramps the autoerase brightness from 0 (up fade) or 31 (down fade) by A10 every three ticks until it passes 31, calling addbae each step, then DIEs. The step is addbae's; the loop is a process and a SLEEPK.

routines.name: adjust_bar_height
routines.evidence: MENU.ASM:840. Grows or shrinks the operator volume bar one line at a time toward a target, drawing each line through vol_bar_line. The bar is pixels in the frame buffer.

routines.name: adjust_text_position
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It nudges a text plate into place.

routines.name: adjust_tl
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It nudges the top-left of one.

routines.name: anim_mk
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It animates the Mortal Kombat 3 tip screen's icons.

routines.name: anim_sparkle
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It the sparkle that runs along an earned icon.

routines.name: arw_bwait
routines.evidence: The arrow that waits for a button on the between-rounds screen.

routines.name: ask_belt_question
routines.evidence: The 'which belt' prompt between ladder stages. Screen construction; the ladder state it draws is wm/pregame.h's.

routines.name: aud_prtone
routines.evidence: Prints one audit line to the ticket printer via BEGIN_AUDIT and the AUD_ROUTINE pointer in the audit table. A printer this port does not have.

routines.name: audit_icons
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It writes the icon audits to CMOS.

routines.name: audit_ud
routines.evidence: `movi 1,a14 / move a14,@audit_ud_flag / move @GAMSTATE,a14` -- raises the flag that tells the rest of the game an audit update is in flight, then writes the accumulated counters back to CMOS. The counters are the port's; the CMOS write is not.

routines.name: audit_wrestler
routines.evidence: WRESTLE2.ASM. Bumps the per-wrestler CMOS audit counter.

routines.name: award_text
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It the award name strings.

routines.name: background_sound
routines.evidence: The sound test's own noise loop: `clr a3 / calla SNDSND`, then sound_fx_table on a timer forever. It exists to make the operator's sound test audible and is not reachable from the game.

routines.name: bbicon_table
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It the icon image table a bar draws from.

routines.name: bcd2hex
routines.evidence: DIAG.ASM:417. Eight-digit BCD to binary, by repeated mask-multiply-accumulate. Portable arithmetic, but it exists only for the PIC security chip: its two callers (DIAG.ASM:600 and :612) both convert a serial number read out of PIC_COMMAND, and that chip is the cabinet's.

routines.name: begin_ani
routines.evidence: SPECIAL.ASM:1200. Reads a projectile process's XVAL/YVAL/ZVAL/FLAGS/XVEL/YVEL and the first entry of its animation script, then BEGINOBJP. Object creation start to finish.

routines.name: begin_obj
routines.evidence: A BEGINOBJ wrapper -- DMAWNZ|M_SCRNREL flags and an object id.

routines.name: bgnd_addblk
routines.evidence: BAKGND.ASM:576. Allocate an object for a block and link it into the display list, sorted by Z then Y. The DECISION to add it is wm_bgnd_scanmod's, and the ordering rule is already translated as wm/bmod.h's wm_bmod_draw_before; this is the object allocation and the DMA control word, which this port has no object pool for.

routines.name: bin2bcd
routines.evidence: DIAG.ASM:381 _pic_bin2bcd. The inverse, by repeated divide-by-a-descending-power-of-ten. Same three callers, same reason: it formats the PIC serial number for the diagnostics screen.

routines.name: call_wrestler_name
routines.evidence: Starts the announcer saying the name of the wrestler just chosen. The decisions around it are translated elsewhere; the object creation and layout are the display layer's.

routines.name: change_image
routines.evidence: WRESTLE.ASM:4290. Point an object at a new image header: OIMG, OSIZE, OSAG, and the ODXOFF/ODYOFF display offsets read out of the header's IANIOFFX/IANIOFFY. A DMA object's fields, and this port has no object pool. The animation VM reaches the same idea by handing a frame NAME to the backend.

routines.name: change_image_local
routines.evidence: SPECIAL.ASM:1259. special_ani's image write on its own: OIMG, OSIZE, OSAG, the two display offsets and the z-compare byte.

routines.name: civani
routines.evidence: Writes OIMG/OSIZE/OSAG/OCTRL on a display object to swap its image. There is no object system in this port; every animation change ends at a frame-name seam instead.

routines.name: civanic
routines.evidence: civani with the object's existing OCTRL preserved. Same reason.

routines.name: convulse_t
routines.evidence: LIFEBAR.ASM:1863. The same story: nine REFLONGs identical to REACT1.ASM:1856 hitonground_tbl, behind the alias chain `SUBR convulse_t` / `#hitonground`.

routines.name: crd_updatetxt
routines.evidence: `movi CP_PID1,a0 / movi 0ffffh,a1 / calla KILALL` then redraws the credit-page text objects. The operator credit screen's own redraw.

routines.name: create_end_rnd_awards
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It creates the end-of-round award bar.

routines.name: create_impact3
routines.evidence: SPECIAL.ASM:397. Two refusals then a CREATE: `@no_debris` and `@reduce_bog` both abort it outright, which is the same pair wm/arcade/wm_arcade_debris.h already gates on. What is left is the DEBRIS_PID creation at a fixed 58h offset.

routines.name: create_player_awards
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It creates one player's award objects.

routines.name: dan_test
routines.evidence: A developer's test page, reachable only from the diagnostic menu. The attract sequence's order and timing are wm/arcade/wmania_attract_core.h's; these build the pages.

routines.name: del_bonus_icons
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It deletes them again.

routines.name: del_progress_icon
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It deletes one of those.

routines.name: delay_code_a3
routines.evidence: The DCS sound board's own protocol. An N64 has no ADSP-2105 and no sample ROM to drive with it; what crosses the boundary instead is the 16-bit CALL the board would have been handed, which wm/arcade/wm_arcade_sound.h's mixer decides on and wm/audio.h's queue carries to the platform. A send_code_a3 with a delay in front of it, for calls the board needs spacing between.

routines.name: direction_test
routines.evidence: WRESTLE.ASM:4714. A development harness: BEGINOBJ a D2ST2B03 marker at one wrestler and fly it to another over TSEC ticks, with the X and Z velocities divided out by hand, to show which way something is pointing. It is not `dead` -- it has exactly one reference, and that reference is its OWN `CREATE 0,direction_test` at :4723, carrying the source's comment "temp!!!!!!!!!!!" and sitting inside the `.if 0` that wraps the routine's whole first half. So nothing in the built game reaches it, but the reference count is 1 rather than 0 and calling it dead would be false. What it does is make an object, which this port has no renderer for.

routines.name: dirq_wait
routines.evidence: `move @dirqtimer,a0` then spins until the display interrupt has bumped it. A busy-wait on an interrupt this port does not take.

routines.name: display_blank
routines.evidence: UTIL.ASM. Turns the display processor off. There is no display processor.

routines.name: display_croutons
routines.evidence: Puts the small per-player marker objects up for whichever players PSTATUS says are in. The decisions around it are translated elsewhere; the object creation and layout are the display layer's.

routines.name: display_dufus_message
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It draws one dufus message box.

routines.name: dizzy_proc
routines.evidence: SPECIAL.ASM:158. The star process create_dizzy_proc spawns: orbit the wrestler's head until STARS_FLAG clears, then die.

routines.name: dma_irq
routines.evidence: The DMA completion interrupt service routine -- `move -*b14,-*b12,L` unwinding the B-file registers it saved. An interrupt handler for a blitter this port does not have.

routines.name: dma_wait
routines.evidence: `move @DMACTRL,b0 / jrn dwlp` -- spins on the blitter's busy bit.

routines.name: dmaq_wait
routines.evidence: Blanks the display, waits for the DMA queue to drain, and unblanks. Same blitter.

routines.name: do_rr_vs
routines.evidence: Draws the royal-rumble versus screen from the two logo images index1 and index2 name. Screen construction; the ladder state it draws is wm/pregame.h's.

routines.name: do_win_streaks
routines.evidence: LIFEBAR.ASM:2164 -- build the two-digit win-streak display for each player: clamp to 99, BINBCD, index #f_t for each nibble's digit image and BEGINOBJ it at a fixed screen position, plus the `lwin` label object. It reads p1winstreak/p2winstreak and writes only objects.

routines.name: dpageflip_off
routines.evidence: `clr a0 / move a0,@dpageflip / not a0` -- clears the page-flip flag and returns its old value so a caller can put it back. One flag; the port renders single-buffered through libdragon and has no equivalent to restore.

routines.name: draw_beaten_table_entry
routines.evidence: The same row draw for the games-beaten table. The row selection and ordering are wmania_hiscore_present.h's wm_hs_present_rows; what is left here is the object creation and the font and palette choices, which are the text layer's.

routines.name: draw_combo_meter
routines.evidence: Draws the combo bar at a given size.

routines.name: draw_each_beaten_table_entry
routines.evidence: Walks the beaten table calling draw_beaten_table_entry per visible row. The row selection and ordering are wmania_hiscore_present.h's wm_hs_present_rows; what is left here is the object creation and the font and palette choices, which are the text layer's.

routines.name: draw_each_inter_table_entry
routines.evidence: Walks the intercontinental table the same way. The row selection and ordering are wmania_hiscore_present.h's wm_hs_present_rows; what is left here is the object creation and the font and palette choices, which are the text layer's.

routines.name: draw_letter_grid
routines.evidence: Lays the A-Z entry grid out for the initials screen. The row selection and ordering are wmania_hiscore_present.h's wm_hs_present_rows; what is left here is the object creation and the font and palette choices, which are the text layer's.

routines.name: draw_mugshot
routines.evidence: Creates the eight image pieces of a wrestler's mugshot into #MUG1..#MUG8 in the process's own PDATA. The decisions around it are translated elsewhere; the object creation and layout are the display layer's.

routines.name: draw_pinspeed_table_entry
routines.evidence: Draws one pin-speed row: initials at [Y,Xleft], the time at [Y,Xright] through val_to_dec_tenths_asc, in palette a11. The row selection and ordering are wmania_hiscore_present.h's wm_hs_present_rows; what is left here is the object creation and the font and palette choices, which are the text layer's.

routines.name: draw_tag_table_entry
routines.evidence: The same row draw for the tag table. The row selection and ordering are wmania_hiscore_present.h's wm_hs_present_rows; what is left here is the object creation and the font and palette choices, which are the text layer's.

routines.name: draw_winstreak_table_entry
routines.evidence: The same row draw for the win-streak table. The row selection and ordering are wmania_hiscore_present.h's wm_hs_present_rows; what is left here is the object creation and the font and palette choices, which are the text layer's.

routines.name: dufus_msg_off
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It turns it off.

routines.name: dufus_msg_on
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It turns a dufus message on.

routines.name: dufus_msgs
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It the dufus message table.

routines.name: erase_mugshot
routines.evidence: Deletes those eight, walking the same PDATA slots. The decisions around it are translated elsewhere; the object creation and layout are the display layer's.

routines.name: fallbacks_t
routines.evidence: LIFEBAR.ASM:1849. Nine REFLONGs, and they are the SAME nine as REACT1.ASM:1801 fall_back_tbl -- hrt_fall_back_anim down to lex_fall_back_anim with slot 7 empty. Already extracted under that name into src/generated/roster_anim_tables.c. tools/wlrostertbl.py does not see this copy because three labels stand in a row above the rows (`SUBR fallbacks_t`, then `#fallbacks_t`, then `#fall_back`) and its reader stops at the second. Teaching it to walk an alias chain was tried and reverted: it misattributed rows across the tree and cost fourteen tables that were being read correctly, for two whose contents are already here.

routines.name: fastanic
routines.evidence: ROPES.ASM:558 -- point a DMA object at a new image: ODOFF, OIMG, OSIZE, OSAG and the five z-compare bits of OCTRL, plus a CALLERR if the image pointer is below ROM. Every line writes the object hardware and there is nothing else in it.

routines.name: flash_2ndwind

routines.name: flash_bar_icons

routines.name: game_loop

The loop itself is the one structure a port is expected to replace; what it CALLED in order is translated and is the order wm_match_tick runs in.

The value it draws, PLT_CLIFE, is real and is wm_life_inc_life's; the drawing is not.

routines.name: update_name
routines.evidence: Looks the chosen wrestler up through scramble_table and redraws his name plate. The decisions around it are translated elsewhere; the object creation and layout are the display layer's.

routines.name: update_timer
routines.evidence: WRESTLE2.ASM:4370. Reads the two match_time digits, indexes digit_tbl for each one's image and hands it to change_image against the two PDATA object pointers. The clock value itself is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_round.h's; this is the two digits on screen.

routines.name: vol_bar_line
routines.evidence: MENU.ASM:866. Plots one line of the volume bar with cvxyl and a byte-store loop, skipping pixels that already hold the text colour -- the source's own "won't overwrite green pixels (text)", which the code actually tests against ROBO_BLUE after a commented-out ROBO_GREEN. Direct frame-buffer writes.

routines.name: wait_but
routines.evidence: Sleeps until a button is pressed or the page's time runs out. The attract sequence's order and timing are wm/arcade/wmania_attract_core.h's; these build the pages.

routines.name: wrestler_counter
routines.evidence: WRESTLE2.ASM:4045. Sets @wrestler_count to 8 and then builds the on-screen "N remaining" display -- two BEGINOBJP text objects whose X shifts by [11ah,0] when only player 2 is in, and the loop that redraws them as the count falls. The count itself belongs to the 8-on-1 and royal-rumble modes, neither of which exists here (wm/arcade/wm_arcade_mode_dead.h sets out why), so both the value and its display are unreachable.

routines.name: wrestler_main
routines.evidence: One wrestler's process: the endless SLEEPK-1 loop that calls read_switches, calc_closest, the control layer, veladd, friction, set_collision_boxes, confine_wrestler and the animation, once a tick. Every one of those is translated and wm_match_tick calls them in that order for every actor; what is not here is the process wrapper, because there are no processes. WRESTLE.ASM:2820 reset_start2 is the same list written out straight, which is what it was checked against.

routines.name: zero_combo_meter
routines.evidence: Empties a player's combo meter graphic; the combo COUNT itself is wm/arcade/wm_arcade_combo.h's.

routines.name: zip_award_bar
routines.evidence: AWARD.ASM's display half. The award CONDITIONS -- which icon is earned, when, and by whom -- are translated in wm/award.h and run on the real call sites; this is the object and text drawing that shows them, which this port has no renderer for. It slides the award bar on and off.
